doubleDigSequenceV1:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE three-panel horizontal instructional illustration for The Vegetable Guru, a practical gardening book. Transparent background, wide 3:1 canvas. NO text, labels, numbers, arrows, borders or watermark. EXACTLY THREE equally sized separate panels with generous clear gaps and safe outer margins. All tools wholly visible.
Images 1 and 2 are authoritative HOUSE STYLE references, not subjects. Broad clean dimensional vector-like colour planes, controlled shadows and cream highlight strokes, no black outlines, no tiny stippling or fine texture. Translate this style to warm-brown soil, slightly darker brown lower soil, very dark brown compost, wooden handles and forest-green/grey metal tools. Image 3 is ONLY a composition reference for the three small soil blocks; replace its one-depth process with DOUBLE DIGGING described here. Simplify its excessive soil speckling.
Each panel is a low three-quarter cutaway of the SAME rectangular unframed soil bed, topsoil roughly one spade blade thick above a lower layer of similar thickness. NO timber sides, plants, cardboard, gravel drainage layer or pots. The first removed topsoil is reserved in a small pile BESIDE the bed and remains there in ALL THREE panels.
LEFT: opening a trench across the NEAR end of the bed, one spade blade deep. Topsoil removed and piled beside bed. Flat visible trench bottom in lower soil. Complete digging spade leaning beside pile. Sparse compost on the remaining undug surface.
CENTRE: the SAME first trench, with topsoil still removed. Show a strong FOUR-TINED garden FORK planted at a gentle angle INTO THE FLOOR OF THE TRENCH, with its tines penetrating a SECOND fork depth into the lower layer. The cross-section makes this downward penetration visible. Broad cracks/clods around the tines show the lower layer being loosened IN PLACE, small dark compost clumps worked into it. The fork head is BELOW the original trench floor and its shaft rises out of the trench. NO second topsoil excavation, NO subsoil pile above ground, NO spade in this panel. The loosening raises the floor a little but leave trench clearly visible.
RIGHT: work progressing along the bed. The previous near-end trench has been refilled with warm-brown TOPSOIL, above loosened lower soil. An adjacent open trench is now present just behind it; a full spade carries warm-brown topsoil from this next strip TOWARDS the filled near strip. Keep the darker lower soil beneath the topsoil. Reserved first-trench soil remains in a small separate pile to the side. Show coarse loosened lower soil below the filled strip, and still unloosened soil below the new open trench, since that is forked next.
The critical distinction is loosening the LOWER layer with a fork while returning TOPSOIL to the upper layer. This is a schematic explanation, not realistic textured landscaping. Make all three stages strong and readable at 160mm overall printed width.
smotherSequenceV1:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE wide, two-panel explanatory illustration of TEMPORARY TARPAULIN SMOTHERING for The Vegetable Guru gardening book, transparent background, landscape approximately 3:1. No lettering, numbers, arrows, labels, borders or watermark. The two panels are equally sized, clearly separate with a generous transparent gap, all complete shapes within safe outer margins. No people.
Reference images 1 and 2 are the approved HOUSE STYLE only, not subjects: bold simplified dimensional vector-like shapes, broad overlapping colour and shadow planes, cream highlight slashes, no heavy black outlines, no photographic textures, no tiny speckles or naturalistic detail. Reference image 3 supplies ONLY the soil/tool visual continuity of the existing book diagrams. Draw ground and props in this family but keep surface texture simpler. Warm brown soil, saturated dark forest-green tarp, green grass, warm grey stones and wooden-handled muted steel garden rake.
LEFT PANEL: an oblong patch of close-cut grass seen from low three-quarter overhead. OPAQUE dark forest-green tarpaulin lies flat and covers the ENTIRE rectangular growing footprint, all corners down, its whole perimeter held down with a series of clearly visible modest grey stones. Show a little close-cut green grass OUTSIDE the tarpaulin edges. Tarp is solid opaque sheet, with a few large simple folds and cream highlights. It is a temporary light-blocking cover, not netting, cardboard or a timber-sided bed. No holes, plants or growing crops through it.
RIGHT PANEL: same patch at a LATER TIME after the cover has been removed and neatly rolled BESIDE the patch. The bare warm-brown ground has only a few pale straw-brown limp dead weeds lying FLAT on it, being raked towards one small pile near the edge. A complete rake rests diagonally beside the patch with head on the surface. Several stones set aside beside rolled tarp. No growing green weeds underneath, no plants through the tarp. Same small fringe of green grass outside the footprint. No exaggerated soil cutaway, artificial layers or raised frame.
Instructional meaning is COVER TO EXCLUDE LIGHT, then REMOVE COVER AND CLEAR DEAD GROWTH. All opaque tarp in first panel and rolled removed tarp in second must be unambiguous. Attractive compact coherent group at about 120–150mm printed width.
